chunks: Tawaf al-Ziyadah is called ziyarah because the pilgrim comes from Mina to visit the House, does not stay in Mecca, and rather returns to Mina.

It is preferable that he perform tawaf of the House on the Day of Sacrifice after completing the rites of Mina; if that is not possible, then on the eleventh day. It should not be delayed beyond that, and it has been said to be prohibited, as in Rawdat al-Mutayaqin.

key_terms.الْحُرْمَةِ: Prohibition; the view that delaying it beyond the mentioned time is forbidden.
key_terms.تَأْخِيرُهُ: Its postponement beyond the preferred or allowed time.
key_terms.زِيَارَةً: Visitation; the name given to this tawaf because the pilgrim comes to visit the Sacred House and returns.
key_terms.طَوَافُ الزِّيَادَةِ: The additional tawaf performed as part of the hajj rites after returning from Mina.
key_terms.مَنَاسِكِ مِنًى: The prescribed rites performed in Mina during hajj.
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice, the preferred time for this tawaf.

ai.seo_question: When should Tawaf al-Ziyadah be performed during hajj, and why is it called ziyarah?
ai.summary: This passage explains why Tawaf al-Ziyadah is also called ziyarah and clarifies its preferred timing in the hajj rites. It indicates that performing it on Yawm al-Nahr after the rites of Mina is best, and if not possible then on the eleventh day, with delaying it further regarded as impermissible by some scholars.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: The "Tawaf al-Ziyadah" is called "Ziyara" (visitation) because the pilgrim comes from Mina to visit the Sacred House but does not stay in Mecca and returns to Mina afterward.

It is preferable for the pilgrim to perform this tawaf on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) after completing the rites of Mina. If that is not possible, it should be performed on the eleventh day. It should not be delayed beyond this, and some scholars, such as in Rawdat al-Mutayaqin, have stated that delaying it is prohibited.
